guide_line: A metal loses electrons, a nonmetal gains them, and the ion charges in the formula add to zero.
steps: A metal atom loses valence electrons and becomes a positive ion, a cation. A nonmetal atom gains electrons and becomes a negative ion, an anion.
Main-group metals lose enough electrons to match the previous noble gas. Group 1 ions are 1+, group 2 ions are 2+, and aluminum is 3+.
Nonmetals gain enough electrons to match the next noble gas. Group 17 ions are 1−, group 16 ions are 2−, and group 15 ions are 3−.
The compound is neutral. Choose the smallest whole-number counts so the total positive charge equals the total negative charge. Write the cation first.
When a molar mass is requested, add the OpenStax atomic masses with every digit kept, then round the final mass to 4 significant figures.

worked_example.q: Potassium and sulfur form an ionic compound. What is its formula?
steps: Potassium is in group 1, so the ion is K+.
Sulfur is in group 16, so the ion is S2−.
Two K+ ions cancel one S2− ion.

similar_problem.q: What is the formula of calcium nitride?
similar_problem.hint: Calcium is 2+ and nitride is 3−. Three calcium ions and two nitride ions make the charges add to zero.

problems.q: What is the formula of calcium nitride?
problems.why: Ca is 2+ and N is 3−. Three Ca2+ give +6 and two N3− give −6. The neutral formula is Ca3N2.
hints: Calcium is 2+ and nitride is 3−. Three calcium ions and two nitride ions make the charges add to zero.

problems.q: What is the charge on a potassium ion? Use a sign, such as 1+ or 2−.
problems.why: Potassium is in group 1 and has one valence electron. It loses that electron, so the ion is K+ with charge 1+.
hints: Potassium sits in group 1 and has a single valence electron to lose.

problems.q: What is the charge on an oxide ion? Use a sign, such as 1− or 2−.
problems.why: Oxygen is in group 16 and has six valence electrons. It gains two electrons to match neon, so oxide is O2−.
hints: Oxygen has six valence electrons and needs two more to reach a full outer shell.

problems.q: What is the charge on an aluminum ion? Use a sign, such as 2+ or 3+.
problems.why: Aluminum is in group 13 and has three valence electrons. It loses all three, so the ion is Al3+.
hints: Aluminum is in group 13. Count those three valence electrons and remove all of them.

problems.q: What is the formula of sodium oxide?
problems.why: Na+ is 1+ and O2− is 2−. Two sodium ions balance one oxide ion, so the formula is Na2O.
hints: Each sodium ion is only 1+. An oxide ion is 2−, so count how many sodium ions that takes.

problems.q: What is the formula of magnesium chloride?
problems.why: Mg2+ is 2+ and each Cl− is 1−. Two chloride ions balance one magnesium ion. The formula is MgCl2.
hints: Magnesium forms a 2+ ion. Each chloride is 1−, so the formula needs more than one chlorine.

problems.q: What is the formula of magnesium nitride?
problems.why: Mg2+ and N3− need a common total of 6. Three magnesium ions and two nitride ions give Mg3N2.
hints: Magnesium is 2+ and nitride is 3−. Find the smallest counts whose charges cancel. This pair is not 1 and 1.

problems.q: What is the formula of calcium oxide?
problems.why: Ca2+ and O2− already have equal and opposite charges. One of each gives the formula CaO.
hints: Calcium and oxide both carry a charge of size 2, so the ratio is not 2 to 1.

problems.q: What is the formula of aluminum sulfide?
problems.why: Al3+ and S2− cross to two aluminums and three sulfides. The charges are +6 and −6. The formula is Al2S3.
hints: Aluminum is 3+ and sulfide is 2−. Cross those charge numbers to choose the subscripts.

problems.why: Magnesium is a metal and chlorine is a nonmetal. Magnesium gives electrons to chlorine, so MgCl2 is ionic.
hints: Look at magnesium first. It is a metal paired with a halogen, which is the transfer case.

problems.why: Magnesium is a metal and oxygen is a nonmetal. The ions are Mg2+ and O2−, so MgO is ionic.
hints: Oxygen can share electrons with other nonmetals, but the partner here is the metal magnesium.

problems.why: Mg(NO3)2 is made of Mg2+ and two NO3− ions. The attraction between those ions is ionic, even though the bonds inside nitrate are covalent.
hints: Split the formula into a metal ion and nitrate ions before you decide. The link between those ions is the one to classify.

problems.q: Use the OpenStax atomic masses Mg = 24.3050 and Cl = 35.4527. What is the molar mass of MgCl2, in g/mol, to 4 significant figures?
problems.why: 24.3050 + 2(35.4527) = 24.3050 + 70.9054 = 95.2104. Rounded to 4 significant figures, the molar mass is 95.21 g/mol.
hints: Add the magnesium mass to two chlorine masses. Do not round either mass before you add.

problems.q: Use Mg = 24.3050, N = 14.0067, and O = 15.9994. What is the molar mass of Mg(NO3)2, in g/mol, to 4 significant figures?
problems.why: The formula contains 1 Mg, 2 N, and 6 O. 24.3050 + 2(14.0067) + 6(15.9994) = 24.3050 + 28.0134 + 95.9964 = 148.3148, which is 148.3 g/mol to 4 significant figures.
hints: The subscript after the parentheses applies to both N and O. Count six oxygens, not three.

problems.q: Write the electron configuration of Mg2+. A noble-gas core is fine.
problems.why: A magnesium atom is [Ne] 3s2. The Mg2+ ion loses both 3s electrons, so the configuration is [Ne], or 1s2 2s2 2p6.
hints: A neutral magnesium atom ends in 3s2. The ion has lost both of those electrons.

problems.q: Write the electron configuration of Cl−. A noble-gas core is fine.
problems.why: A chlorine atom is [Ne] 3s2 3p5. The chloride ion gains one electron and fills 3p, so the configuration is [Ar], or 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6.
hints: Chlorine’s 3p subshell has five electrons. The anion fills that subshell.

problems.q: Write the electron configuration of Na+. A noble-gas core is fine.
problems.why: A sodium atom is [Ne] 3s1. Na+ loses that one 3s electron, so the configuration is [Ne], or 1s2 2s2 2p6.
hints: Sodium has one electron past neon. The cation loses only that electron.

problems.q: What is the formula of aluminum oxide?
problems.why: Aluminum forms Al3+ and oxygen forms O2−. Two aluminum ions are 6+, and three oxide ions are 6−. The formula is Al2O3.
hints: Aluminum is 3+ and oxide is 2−. Use two aluminum ions and three oxide ions so the charges cancel.

problems.q: What is the formula of sodium nitride?
problems.why: Sodium forms Na+ and nitrogen forms N3−. Three sodium ions balance one nitride ion. The formula is Na3N.
hints: Sodium is 1+ and nitride is 3−. Only three sodium ions cancel one nitride ion.
